eyebrow: A PRAYER SERIES ON YOUR CHILDREN
coverTitle:
Five Prayers
For The Child
You Can't Stop Worrying About
coverDek: For the 2am scroll through their messages, the call you're still waiting on, and the prayer you keep repeating like it hasn't been heard yet — five prayers for the parent who loves too much to stop worrying.

points.hook: Lord, I didn't know loving someone could feel this much like holding your breath.
paragraphs: I check my phone more than I'd like to admit, just to see if they've texted back. I replay our last conversation looking for the moment I said the wrong thing. Lord, I didn't know loving a child this much could feel this much like fear — teach me to trade the worry for the prayer, one more time tonight.
points.verseText: Train up a child in the way he should go: and when he is old, he will not depart from it.

points.hook: I decree over my child: every voice that is not Yours will lose its hold.
paragraphs: I decree over my child, in the name of Jesus: every wrong voice trying to raise them instead of me will lose its grip — every wrong friend, every wrong door, every wrong idea of who they are! What the enemy whispers to them in private, I cancel out loud. My child belongs to the Lord, and great shall be their peace!
points.verseText: And all thy children shall be taught of the LORD; and great shall be the peace of thy children.

points.hook: Notice what the worry over your child is doing to your own shoulders tonight.
paragraphs: Notice your shoulders right now — how high they're sitting, how long you've been carrying them like that. Worry about your child doesn't just live in your mind, it lives in your clenched jaw and your shallow breathing and the sleep you keep losing over a phone that hasn't rung. Lord, let me hand You what I keep holding in my body, not just in my prayers.
points.verseText: Be careful for nothing; but in every thing by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known unto God.

points.hook: Somebody's child is walking a road tonight that their parent doesn't even know about.
paragraphs: Family, somebody here has a child walking a road right now that you don't even know the name of — a choice, a friend group, a quiet struggle they haven't told you. You are not the only one lying awake over a child you can't reach tonight. Agree with someone else in this family: the Lord who said He would contend with what contends against your household is still fighting for that child, even from here.
points.verseText: I will contend with him that contendeth with thee, and I will save thy children.

points.hook: Child, I love your child more than you do, and I have never once lost sight of them.
paragraphs: Child, I love the one you're worrying over more than you do, and I have not lost sight of them for a single second — not on the nights they're with you, and not on the nights they're somewhere you can't follow. I am not finished writing their story. Let go of what you were never meant to carry alone, and rest tonight.
points.verseText: It is not the will of your Father which is in heaven, that one of these little ones should perish.

cta.closingLine: If even one of these named the child you've been carrying in prayer, don't carry it alone tonight — come back tomorrow for the next series.
